newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wooltru new listings seen by Sept/Oct.
newsitem.headline: Wooltru new listings seen by Sept/Oct.

text.p: Wooltru subsidiaries Woolworths and Truworths International could be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange by September or October, executive chairman Colin Hall said on Thursday.

Briefing the media and brokers on the retail group's unexpectedly strong interim results, Hall said the board was still considering the right percentage of shares to issue for tradeability and the structure of the shares.
"It is more likely to be in the second half of the year, in September or October," Hall said.
The group already had N and ordinary shares and would have to consider whether the subsidiaries should have them as well.
"There is some difficulty with regard to how you deal with that. N shares are not very palatable."
There might also be staff share schemes and all these would be finalised over the next few months.
Hall announced that in the six months to December 31, 1996, earnings per share rose 23 percent to 61.9 cents from 50.3 cents while the interim dividend rose 22 percent to 22 cents from 18 cents.
"The results for the half year are a pretty clear indication that we are firing on all cylinders," Hall said.
As a result, the next phase would be to allowing the subsidiaries to "become part of the big world" though a listing.
But Wooltru was "not in an unbundling mood...Wooltru has added value over the years, it has learnt how to add that value at a relatively low cost and it can do that again."
